subject: Post-call: defining streaming tail latency, throughput, and remedies
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodai.com>
To: Tom Miller <tom.miller@heliosretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: defining streaming tail latency, throughput, and remedies

Thanks again for the call this morning — good discussion and clear priorities. I captured the main performance items we need to lock down for the pilot and the SLA:

- Latency measurement: you called out that tail latency for interactive search must be tight. We need to confirm whether Helios wants p99 on full-response completion, token-stream tail, or both.
- Throughput / concurrency: please confirm expected peak QPS and concurrent active streams per region (you estimated ~4k concurrent globally on the call).
- Streaming behavior: requirements for chunk size, partial-response semantics (do you treat the first partial token as a measurable success?), and keepalive/idle timeouts.
- Reporting & cadence: weekly dashboard vs. monthly SLA statement; retention of logs for audits.
- Exclusions & remedies: maintenance windows, retries, user-side network issues, and how credits should be calculated (minutes of degradation vs number of failed requests).

Attached is a first-pass SLO draft (Redwood_SLO-draft-v1.pdf) that maps our runtime metrics to candidate SLA language. Highlights in the draft: p95/p99 buckets, separate measurements for streaming-completion and token-latency, suggested 30s cure period for transient infra events, and a proposed credit schedule.

Next steps / asks from Helios: please confirm the following by EOD Thursday so we can iterate the SLA wording with Legal/Rev Ops:
- Which latency percentile(s) are binding for interactive flows (p95 / p99 / p999)?
- Do you require p99 on response-complete and p99 on last-token-stream, or only the former?
- Peak concurrency and sustained throughput (QPS) per region and by hour.
- Acceptance of our proposed exclusions (maintenance windows, scheduled upgrades, DDoS, third-party provider outages).

Internal follow-up: looping in Ben to help with the remedies/legal language once Helios confirms the above. Karthik — please flag any immediate compatibility concerns on the runtime side (prefix caching, tokenization/cost, or concurrent stream limits).

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Rachel.Kim@redwoodai.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_SLO-draft-v1.pdf (short draft, sections 1-4)
From: Tom Miller <tom.miller@heliosretail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@heliosretail.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: defining streaming tail latency, throughput, and remedies

Thanks Rachel — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Binding metrics: for customer-facing interactive search we prefer p99 on response completion (time until the final token is sent). However, we also care about streaming smoothness and would like telemetry on token-stream intervals (token-to-token gaps) at p95 so we can detect stalls.
- If we must choose one binding number initially, make it p99 on response completion.
- Concurrency/throughput: our expected peak is ~4,500 concurrent active streams during peak hours (US east), with sustained QPS of ~1,200 and spikes up to 2,500 for short bursts (Holiday-like traffic). We'll provide hourly traffic histograms by Thursday.
- Streaming semantics: partial results are valid (we show progressive results in the UI), but a response is considered complete only when the final EOS token is delivered (or the stream closes). We also want a max per-stream idle timeout of 90s before Redwood closes the socket.
- Reporting cadence: weekly health dashboard (near-real-time) + a monthly SLA statement in PDF for procurement/audit.

On exclusions: we accept scheduled maintenance with at least 48 hours notice. For third-party cloud provider outages, we need a clear definition (e.g., region-level provider outage recognized by provider status page).

Attaching our SRE requirements for reference (Helios-SRE-requirements.pdf). One ask from our Security team: we need logs retained for 90 days for any SLA incident.

Tom Miller
Head of Platform Engineering, Helios Retail
Tom.Miller@heliosretail.com
Attachment: Helios-SRE-requirements.pdf
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodai.com>
To: Tom Miller <tom.miller@heliosretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: defining streaming tail latency, throughput, and remedies

Appreciate the quick clarifications, Tom — that helps a lot. A few notes and proposed refinements based on your input:

1) Measurement definitions (proposed for the SLA text)
   - Response-complete latency (binding): measured at server egress — time from first request byte received by Redwood to final byte of the response leaving Redwood's egress interface. Percentiles: p50/p95/p99. Binding SLA will use p99 on response-complete as requested.
   - Streaming smoothness (informational): token-interval gaps measured at server-side between consecutive token packets; report p50/p95 to surface stalls. Not binding initially, but will be included in weekly dashboard.

2) Exclusions (proposed)
   - Scheduled maintenance (>=48 hours notice)
   - Force majeure and third-party provider outages (must be documented against provider status page)
   - Customer client/network issues (we will provide last-mile diagnostics; if packet loss is observed on client-side, that instance is excluded)

3) Reporting cadence & retention
   - Weekly: near-real-time dashboard with p95/p99 for response-complete and token-gap histograms.
   - Monthly: signed PDF SLA statement showing monthly aggregates, incidents, and any applied credits.
   - Logs retained for 90 days for any incident (Helios SRE request) — we can provide log export links and raw request traces on-demand.

4) Remedies (initial proposal)
   - Degradation credit formula: for each calendar month, if measured p99 response-complete exceeds the guaranteed threshold for more than X minutes aggregated (we propose X=60 minutes), Redwood will issue service credits equal to (minutes degraded / total minutes in month) * monthly committed fee * 0.25.
   - Cure period: 30 minutes for transient infra blips; sustained degradations after cure period count toward minutes degraded.

5) Throughput & concurrency operational notes
   - We can provision a Dedicated pool sized for 4,500 concurrent active streams (US east) as a reserved capacity option; for Hosted we’ll configure autoscaling + burst to handle the 2,500 short spikes.
   - We recommend soft-limits per account to protect multi-tenant environments; we’ll share a concurrency-safe rollout plan.

Next steps:
- Tom/Elena: please confirm acceptance of the measurement definitions, proposed exclusions, log retention, and the remedies formula above.
- Karthik/Infra: internal check on whether 90s idle timeout and the proposed concurrency targets require any kernel tuning or increased KV cache sizing.
- Ben: if you can draft suggested contract language (short clause) for the remedies and exclusions we can send a redline to Helios procurement.

Thanks — will do a follow-up demo of streaming behavior with a simulated peak tomorrow if that helps.

Rachel Kim
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Rachel.Kim@redwoodai.com

Attachment: Redwood_SLO-draft-v1.pdf (updated with measurement defs)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodai.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodai.com>, Tom Miller <tom.miller@heliosretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 18:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: defining streaming tail latency, throughput, and remedies

Looping in Legal/Contracts and sharing a few redline suggestions for the SLA clause. I attached a doc with tracked changes (SLA-language-redlines.docx). High-level points:

- Remedies: recommend simpler cap language for credits — cap total monthly credits at 50% of monthly committed fees to limit exposure for very large outages.
- Measurement: tie measurements to Redwood's telemetry (server egress metrics) but allow Helios the right to request raw traces for disputes (we can provide within 7 business days).
- Cure period & aggregation: agree on a 30m cure, but require aggregating contiguous degraded intervals separated by less than 15 minutes to be considered one incident for credit calculation.
- Exclusions: add explicit exclusion for customer-initiated load testing and exceedance of agreed rate-limits; add placeholder for maintenance blackout windows.

If this looks reasonable, I’ll prepare a one-page SLA exhibit to append to the master services agreement and send to your procurement contact.

Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodai.com
Attachment: SLA-language-redlines.docx
